title: Traffic Escalator: Multi-Signal Rollout Gates with Deterministic Auto-Rollback
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Goal: Ship a deterministic, observable "traffic escalator" subsystem that combines multiple health signals into gating decisions for progressive delivery. The escalator must support: fine-grained percent ramps, per-customer and global canaries, feature-flag integration, and an auditable auto-rollback state machine. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, and console integration for runtime-1.20.

Motivation: Existing progressive-delivery tooling focuses on single-signal checks (error rate or latency). We need a multi-signal approach to reduce false positives/negatives in rollback decisions as models and serving kernels evolve. The escalator will improve safety for model promotions, quantization rollouts, and LTS channel migrations while maintaining fast promotion for low-risk changes.
acceptance_criteria: Escalator service calculates a composite canary score from configured signals (P99 latency, 95th latency, 5xx rate, token loss ratio, queue depth growth) and exposes a decision endpoint.
Default rollout policy implemented: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 30% -> 100% with configurable hold windows and backoff on marginal stability.
Auto-rollback triggers when composite score crosses configured thresholds for two consecutive evaluation windows, and rollback action is executed without manual intervention.
Feature-flag gating works end-to-end: enabling the flag triggers an escalator run, and disabling it immediately halts progression and drains canary traffic.
All rollout decisions and state transitions are recorded in audit logs with user/automation identity and linked to the rollout ID.
Console shows rollout progress (percent, hold time remaining, last evaluation) and a synthesized health timeline derived from the escalator signals.
E2E tests simulate success and failure modes with injected faults (latency spikes, error bursts) and validate rollback behavior.
Runbook and post-mortem template added for manual interventions and failed promotions.
implementation_notes: Add 'escalator' microservice (stateless-controller) responsible for scheduling percent ramps, evaluating signals, and issuing routing changes via existing traffic-router API.
Implement composite scoring function with configurable weights and signal normalization; default weights to emphasize P99 and 5xx.
Extend routing-layer API to accept staged allocations (canary set id, pct) and a TTL tag for automatic rollback if heartbeat stops.
Feature-flag integration: require SDK change to surface rollout-id and stage metadata to requests for per-customer sharding and attribution.
Audit: write transitions to existing event-sink (kafka topic 'rollout-events') with structured fields (rollout_id, stage, decision, reason-code).
Backoff & retry: exponential backoff with jitter for advancing to next stage; configurable max retries before marking rollout 'needs-attention'.
LTS promotion mode: when promoting to an LTS channel, enforce stricter thresholds and require a minimum canary duration and manual approval step configurable per release channel.
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring normalization and composite calculation across synthetic signal inputs.
Integration test: escalator calls routing API in staging cluster; verify allocations and TTL semantics.
Chaos test: inject latency and 5xx spikes into canary hosts and verify escalator halts and triggers rollback within expected windows.
Load test: run full ramp sequence under production traffic profile in a shadow environment to validate resource usage and timings.
Manual canary dry-run: ops-triggered end-to-end dry-run with no user-facing traffic (shadow) and review of console UI entries.
rollout_policy: Evaluation window: 5m sliding windows, 3 consecutive windows for a pass/fail decision
Backoff: on marginal pass, retry same stage up to 3 times with exponential backoff; on repeated instability mark rollout 'needs-attention' and pause.
Auto-rollback: triggered when composite score > rollback_threshold for 2 consecutive evaluation windows or when any single signal breaches a critical threshold (eg. 5xx > 1% sustained for 2 windows).
Kill-switch: disable feature-flag immediately forces drain of canary allocations and marks rollout aborted; emergency rollback takes precedence even if escalator is offline.
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: 'Escalator Overview' with live rollout table, per-rollout composite score sparkline, and top contributing signals.
Alerts: 'escalator-rollout-failed' (pager) when auto-rollback occurs or rollout marked needs-attention after backoff retries.
SLO probes: synthetic canary requests that exercise common prompt shapes and capture end-to-end percentiles and correctness metrics.
Tracing: add rollout-id to distributed traces so problematic requests can be attributed to a rollout stage.
